newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac to launch judicial reform inquiry.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac to launch judicial reform inquiry.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, fighting his unpopularity with the voters, will make a live television address on Monday on judicial reform.
A presidency statement said Chirac would speak to the nation before the official appointment of a study commission on the justice system on Tuesday.
Chirac pledged on December 12 to initiate a review of judicial independence.

Questioned about a rash of sleaze probes into all of the major political parties including his own Gaullist Rally for the Republic, Chirac said he had instructed the government to set up a commission to review the workings of the justice system.
Presidential aides and supporters have urged him to appear more frequently on television to help him recover from record-low approval ratings.
Just 36 percent of the French people back the conserative Chirac's actions as president, according to the latest Gallup survey for the weekly L'Express, while 52 percent disapproved.

Chirac's ratings have been driven down by public austerity policies and record unemployment of 12.7 percent as well as charges he has not kept promises made during his campaign for the French presidency, which he won in May 1995 elections.
